sections.content:
The EU Blue Card is Germany's main residence permit for highly skilled workers from outside the EU, and it is the cleanest route for Canadians with a degree and a qualifying job offer. It is tied to a specific job rather than a points system, which makes the requirements clearer — but it also means you cannot apply without an employer lined up. The card is typically valid for up to four years.

It also carries unusually strong family and mobility rights. Your spouse can join you without a language requirement and may work immediately, you can move to another EU country after twelve months, and permanent residency comes after 21 to 27 months. That combination is why the Blue Card beats Germany's other permits for most Canadian professionals.
sections.title: What the EU Blue Card Is

sections.content:
The standard 2026 threshold is €50,700 per year, or €4,225 per month — your contracted gross salary must meet or exceed this figure. A reduced threshold of €45,934.20 per year applies to shortage occupations, which include all IT and software roles, and to graduates whose degree was completed within the last three years. These figures rise with average wages and are reset every January.

There is a higher bar for older applicants: from age 45, the immigration authority generally expects around €55,770 unless you can show adequate pension provision. The thresholds are strict — a contract even slightly below the relevant figure will be rejected, so confirm the current year's numbers before you sign anything.
sections.title: Salary Thresholds for 2026

sections.content:
You need a university degree recognised in Germany. Check the anabin database for an H+ rating on your institution; if your Canadian university is not listed, get a Statement of Comparability from the ZAB — about €208 and up to eight weeks. IT specialists have a special route: with at least three years of relevant experience in the last seven years, they can qualify without a degree at the reduced salary threshold.

The job offer has rules too: a binding offer or contract of at least six months, in a role matching your field of qualification. Self-employment does not qualify. For shortage roles at the reduced threshold, the Federal Employment Agency must approve the employment — one extra step, but routine for genuine offers.
sections.title: Qualification and Job Offer Requirements

sections.content:
Canadians apply at the German consulate or embassy, or at the local immigration office if already in Germany on an eligible visa. The application fee is around €110. Prepare your file carefully — passport, degree recognition, the signed contract showing your salary, and proof of health insurance — because incomplete files are the most common cause of delays.

Processing typically takes 21 to 90 days depending on the office and your case. Once approved, you receive the card as a residence permit with your employment conditions printed on it. Changing jobs within Germany needs no permission, although the immigration authority may object during the first twelve months if the new role would not meet Blue Card conditions.
